The Onesimus Director reads the configuration of the Bareos 25 Director: the same resources, directives and syntax in the same files. Directives marked *Onesimus* exist only in the Onesimus Director. Most directives can also be changed from the console with [`configure`](/docs/commands/configure/) or in the Onesimus GUI.

Syntax in brief: a resource is `Type { ... }`, a directive is `Name = value`; names are case-insensitive and spaces in them do not matter (`Maximum Concurrent Jobs` and `MaximumConcurrentJobs` are the same, the console writes `maximumconcurrentjobs`). Strings with spaces go in double quotes, # starts a comment, and `@file` includes another file.

| Resource | Directives | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [Director](director/) | 50 | The Director resource configures the Director daemon itself: its name, password, listen addresses, working directories and global limits. |
| [Client](client/) | 42 | A Client resource describes a File Daemon the Director backs up: where to reach it, how to authenticate, and limits and quotas for its jobs. |
| [Storage](storage/) | 36 | A Storage resource tells the Director how to reach a Storage Daemon and which of its devices and media type to use. |
| [Catalog](catalog/) | 18 | The Catalog resource describes the PostgreSQL database that holds the job, file and volume records. |
| [Job](job/) | 84 | A Job resource describes one unit of work: what to back up (FileSet) from where (Client), to where (Pool, Storage) and when (Schedule), or a restore, verify, copy, migrate, consolidate or admin job. |
| [JobDefs](jobdefs/) | 84 | A JobDefs resource holds defaults for Job resources: a Job with JobDefs = name takes every directive it does not set itself from it. |
| [FileSet](fileset/) | 6 | A FileSet resource says what a backup job saves: the Include blocks list files and plugins with Options blocks for compression, signatures and patterns; Exclude blocks leave things out. |
| [Schedule](schedule/) | 4 | A Schedule resource holds Run directives that say when the jobs that use it start, at which level and with which overrides. |
| [Pool](pool/) | 32 | A Pool resource groups volumes with the same rules: how long their data is kept, how big they get, how they are labeled and recycled. |
| [Messages](messages/) | 17 | A Messages resource routes the messages of jobs and daemons to destinations: the catalog (job log), mail, files, syslog or the console. |
| [Counter](counter/) | 6 | A Counter resource is a numbered variable, mainly used in Label Format of pools to number volumes. |
| [Profile](profile/) | 12 | A Profile resource is a named set of ACLs that Console and User resources refer to, so several consoles share one definition of what they may do. |
| [Console](console/) | 29 | A Console resource is a named login to the Director with its own password and ACLs (or profiles). |
| [User](user/) | 13 | A User resource gives ACLs (or profiles) to a user who logs in through a PAM console. |
